RT by @no_itsmyturn: Mr. Kushner should judge Hamas by its actions, not its words. Since the ceasefire, Hamas and its allies have worked to consolidate their power in Gaza, signaling that they have no serious intention of fully disarming. Complete disarmament would amount to organizational suicide. It would also contradict the "muqawama" ideology at the core of Hamas’s identity. Armed "resistance groups" do not willingly surrender all their weapons, especially when threatened by potential conflict. Disarmament would also leave Hamas vulnerable to an Israeli effort to dismantle it or a challenge from rival anti-Hamas Palestinian factions such as the Popular Forces. Hamas did not survive the war only to relinquish power. Whatever its long-term plan may be, the group will not willingly surrender the military leverage that allows it to remain in control. Moreover, Hamas is not going to hand Netanyahu a significant political victory months before Israeli elections. That is why people should treat Hamas’s disarmament pledge with skepticism until Hamas and its allies disclose a detailed accounting of their entire arsenal in Gaza and submit the decommissioning process to credible independent verification. RT by @hey_itsmyturn: Four Iranian airmen flew toward Qatar. One returned in a coffin. Three disappeared. 🇮🇷🇶🇦 For nearly five months, Iran officially called them missing. Now Tehran says Qatar has been hiding them alive since March. That sudden transformation is the real story. The two Su-24 bombers were shot down near Qatar on March 2. There is no evidence that either aircraft force-landed. No runway emergency, intact airframe or crash site on land was reported. If the three men survived, they almost certainly ejected over the Gulf. That is not impossible. The Su-24’s K-36D escape seats were designed to function even at extremely low altitude. But the aircraft were reportedly flying around 80 feet above the sea when engaged. Survival would have depended on the missile impact, aircraft attitude, parachute deployment and how quickly rescuers reached them. Qatar controlled the airspace, radar picture and surrounding waters. If the pilots entered the sea alive, Qatari forces were probably the first people capable of finding them. So Iran’s accusation is physically plausible. But Tehran has shown nothing to prove it. No photographs. No emergency-beacon data. No intercepted communications. No rescue coordinates. No witnesses. No message from the pilots. No ICRC confirmation. Doha says it invited Iranian investigators in April and received no response. Tehran says its team has spent months waiting for Qatar to let it enter. Someone is not telling the whole story.👀 The pilots may have died at sea. They may have been rescued and detained. Iran may be manufacturing certainty where none exists.
